title: An upload endpoint uses the caller's ID as a path component, and the attacker aims the write at a module the interpreter imports on startup
index_line: T-0084 · FILE_WRITE · image-ID path traversal writes sitecustomize.py, then a training call spawns Python that imports it · python · corroborated
invariant_violated: The datastore treated the caller-supplied image ID as a name inside its directory, but it was a path: it was appended, joined and copied to without ever resolving the result. The escalation assumes something further — that the only files worth writing are the application's own, when a file the language runtime imports at startup turns a data write into code execution.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated PUT to /datastore/image carries an uploaded file and an attacker-chosen image query parameter
the handler appends the file extension and joins the ID onto the datastore image directory
the upload is copied to the resulting path with no check that the resolved destination stays inside the datastore (../../../<dir>/x escapes it)
the attacker chooses a destination the runtime loads by itself — sitecustomize.py in the interpreter's import path — instead of a path the application serves
a training API call spawns a new Python process on the server
the new interpreter imports sitecustomize.py during startup, running the payload before any application code and yielding a shell with the service's privileges

source.http.request.value: PUT /datastore/image with the image query parameter as the path component

sink.file.write.value: LocalDatastore.add_image() / save_label(): shutil.copy() to a path built from the image ID, with no containment check

fs.path.join.value: ID + extension joined onto the datastore directory; a traversal ID resets the join out of the tree

encoding.path.value: the 'image ID' is treated as a name; the filesystem treats it as a path

guard.none.value: no resolve-then-prefix check on the destination, no basename reduction, no dot-prefixed ID rejection (all added by the fix)

preconditions.expr: the MONAI Label API is reachable without authentication
the deployed package predates 0.8.6 / the fix in PR 1915
the datastore write path joins the caller's image ID without resolving containment

success: a file appears outside the datastore directory at a path the attacker named
a newly spawned training process executes the dropped module before application code (shell/callback)
failure_like: the endpoint reduces the ID to a basename or rejects dot-segments (400)
the resolved destination is verified to be inside the datastore image/label directory
false_positive: a 200 from the upload endpoint without a file outside the datastore is not this bug
a file written inside the datastore under a nested name is normal storage behaviour

hazards: any 'ID becomes a filename' upload in a service that can write outside its data directory
the escalation primitive is generic: sitecustomize.py / usercustomize.py (Python), NODE_OPTIONS+require hooks, .pth files, cron.d, PHP auto_prepend_file, JVM agents
root privileges are common because the service runs as root in a container or appliance
non_transfers: uploads that store content under a server-generated opaque ID
services whose runtime does not import from a writable directory at startup

evidence.target: MONAI Label before 0.8.6, PUT /datastore/image (CVE-2026-133968), exploited in the wild from 2026-09

provenance.author: Amazon Threat Intelligence (AWS Security Blog)
provenance.corroborates: in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-133968: agents mapped the API, found an upload endpoint with a filename parameter, confirmed path traversal, wrote files arbitrarily, dropped a Python reverse shell as sitecustomize.py, then triggered a training API endpoint to spawn a new interpreter that imported the payload — reverse shell as root

provenance.author: Project MONAI maintainers (GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94)
provenance.corroborates: code-level root cause: PUT /datastore/image takes a caller-controlled image query parameter as the image ID; LocalDatastore.add_image() appends the extension, joins it onto the datastore directory and writes with shutil.copy(), never checking the resolved path stays inside the datastore; save_label() does the same; fixed in #1915 by resolving and rejecting escapes

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-133968: monailabel before 0.8.6 allows directory traversal with resultant RCE via the image parameter to PUT /datastore/image, exploited in the wild
